hook: Write down a little winter story by ear and catch every past form, from ging and saß to wartete and öffnete.
intro: One small story in twelve sentences, dictated — the Präteritum by ear. A walk in the snowy forest, a shivering little dog, and how it came to stay. Two things are being trained. First, the irregular stems, which you must recognise from their changed vowel with no -te to help you: ging, lag, saß, gab, nahm, trug, riefen, blieb. Second, the endings: no ending in ich/er (ich ging, er saß), -en in the plural (wir riefen) — and the regular -te / -ete with its unstressed final -e (hörte, zitterte, wartete, öffnete, meldete), which is easy to miss when it is spoken fast. Two mixed verbs appear as well: kannte and nannten. Listen for the vowel first, then the ending, and put a comma before und or aber when a new clause with its own subject begins.
tips[0].title: Vowel first
tips[0].text: If you hear a changed vowel where the infinitive has another — ging (gehen), lag (liegen), saß (sitzen), gab (geben), trug (tragen), blieb (bleiben) — it is an irregular past: write the stem you hear, with no -te.
tips[0].check.why: sitzen is irregular: you hear the changed vowel in saß, so there is no -te.
tips[1].title: The quiet -e of the regulars
tips[1].text: wartete, öffnete, meldete: the final -e is short and easy to lose. A regular verb always ends in -te (singular) or -ten (plural); after t, d or n after a consonant it is -ete.
tips[1].check.why: öffnen is regular; after the n following a consonant it takes -ete, with a short final -e that is easy to miss.
tips[2].title: Comma before und / aber with a new subject
tips[2].text: When und or aber starts a new clause with its own subject and verb, a comma goes before it (optional with und, always with aber). The pause you hear is the comma.
tips[2].check.why: aber opens a new clause with its own subject, so a comma always goes right before it.
remember[0]: Irregular: hear the vowel, write no -te. Regular: -te, always.
remember[1]: Comma at the pause before aber (and before und with a new subject).
exam: Writing about what happened in the past is part of the B1 exam — and of every message telling a friend about your week.
